attribution.note: This is the title of Marcus's own 2025 essay, which he lists and recommends rereading in his own post. He wrote it and endorses it.

semantics.note: 'LLMs are unable to stop hallucinating' matches the essay title. 'Can't stop' also suggests a permanent limit that cannot be tested, but the observable core is that LLMs still hallucinate. Treating it as an observation is reasonable.

contract.note: The plain reading (frontier LLMs still hallucinated at non-trivial rates in late 2025) is fair and ordinary. It sets aside the untestable 'inherent' part, which the contract says openly. It is not stretched for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: Vectara benchmark, Nov 2025: Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5, Grok-4 and other frontier models hallucinated in over 10% of summaries. An independent benchmark from the target period.
Same Vectara benchmark: even the best model scored 3.3%, so no tested model had eliminated hallucination.
Sept 2025 paper by OpenAI researchers saying hallucinations persist in state-of-the-art systems. This is developer research and meets the source requirement.
The Deloitte refund incident (Oct 2025) involved GPT-4o and a report from July 2025, so it is only context for whether frontier models still hallucinated.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's plain reading, an independent benchmark (Vectara, Nov 2025) and OpenAI researchers' own paper (Sept 2025) both show leading LLMs still hallucinated at non-trivial rates in late 2025, and no model reached zero. The packet has no contrary evidence. The stronger claim that hallucination can never be eliminated is not scored.
